Seminars
Main content start

Computing on encrypted data: from concept to reality

Event Details:

Thursday, November 12, 2026
4:30pm - 5:30pm PST

Location

STLC 114
United States

This event is open to:

Faculty/Staff
Members
Students

Abstract/Description: 

Computing on encrypted data and more specifically fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) started a new era in cryptography. This new form of cryptography performs computations on encrypted data without a need to first decrypt the data. This enables a whole new class of applications.  A data owner can store encrypted data in the cloud, thus protecting it from data leaks. The cloud can perform operations on the data while remaining oblivious on the actual data or results. Only the data owner with the right decryption key can obtain the results of the calculations.  

From a theoretical concept (with the invention of bootstrapping in 2009 by Gentry at Stanford) taking hours or days to compute, FHE operations can now be calculated in seconds or milliseconds, appearing real-time.  This progress has been made possible by a combination of advancement in optimizing of applications for computing on encrypted data, improvements on the underlying mathematics, and highly efficient mapping of the operations on the processor architectures: CPU, FPGA, GPU and ASIC.

In this seminar, we will report on results obtained in the context of the ERC Advanced grant Belfort and the Darpa DPRIVE project. We will then focus on the current state of the art and report results obtained by our start-up Belfort. AI and ML have become a major application field for computing on encrypted data. ML applications can now run on encrypted data. We will end with research directions for FHE and the need for new FHE friendly computer architectures.

Speaker Bio:

Dr. Ir. Ingrid Verbauwhede is a Professor in the research group COSIC at KU Leuven. She co-founded and is scientific advisor of the start-up Belfort (www.belfortlabs.com) . She is a fellow of IEEE and of IACR. She is a member of the Royal Academy of Belgium. She received the IEEE 2017 Computer Society Technical Achievement Award. She delivered the 2022 IACR distinguished lecture. She received the 2023 IEEE Don Pederson award for “pioneering contributions to energy-efficient and high-performance secure integrated circuits and systems”, the 2024 EDAA Achievement Award and the 2025 FWO excellence prize. She received two EU ERC Advanced Grants (2016, 2021).

She is a pioneer in the field of efficient and secure implementations of cryptographic algorithms on many different platforms: ASIC, FPGA, embedded, and cloud.  With her research, she bridges the gaps between electronics, the mathematics of cryptography, and the security of trusted computing.  Her group owns and operates an advanced electronic security evaluation lab at the KU Leuven. According to Google Scholar she has an H-index of 99. Her list of publications is available: https://www.esat.kuleuven.be/cosic/people/ingrid-verbauwhede/  or https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=ZyG1ZGgAAAAJ&hl=en&oi=ao
